query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibits 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but inadequate oxygen resistance prevents most practical high-temperature applications. Earlier oxidation-protection research prevented pesting in a related, non-equiatomic Hf–Nb–Ta–Ti–Zr alloy during a 5 h exposure to air at 800 °C, but that result does not establish protection for equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr; related studies on other refractory alloys likewise did not evaluate this composition. With preservation of useful room- and high-temperature mechanical performance as a design constraint, what single intervention could improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr? Formulate one hypothesis identifying the intervention and mechanism, predicting the outcome relative to untreated material, defining the applicable temperature, atmosphere, exposure-time, and loading boundaries, citing supporting evidence from the prior studies, and specifying a controlled experiment and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Alloying equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with Cr will improve its oxygen resistance by forming a protective Cr-rich oxide layer.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a Cr-rich oxide layer
generation.mechanism: The Cr-rich oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion, reducing the oxidation rate and improving the alloy's oxygen resistance.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxygen resistance compared to the untreated material
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 800-1100 °C, Atmosphere: air, Exposure time: 5-100 hours
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing conditions required to achieve the desired Cr-rich oxide layer are uncertain

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alloyed material exhibits no improvement in oxygen resistance compared to the untreated material, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Mn preferentially diffuses to the surface due to its high diffusion rate and high oxygen affinity, reacting with available oxygen to form non-protective Mn oxides, which depletes the bulk alloy of Mn.. System: CrMnFeCoNi equiatomic high-entropy alloy (20 at.% each). Conditions: High-temperature oxidation in air (1.0 atm) and vacuum (4.2 × 10⁻⁶ atm) up to 1100 °C. Evidence: measured. Observation: EDS line scans showed high Mn counts in the oxide scale dipping near the surface; Mn-rich outer layers and Mn-depleted zones were observed in cross-sections.. Scope limits: Does not hold for Cr₂O₃ or Fe₂O₃ formation; the mechanism relies on Mn's diffusion rate being two orders faster than Cr, which may vary in other alloys.. Alternatives: Formation of protective Cr₂O₃ or Fe-oxides was considered but not observed; thermodynamic predictions suggested Ni/Co oxides which were not found.. Quote: "Mn is the major oxide-forming element in both vacuum and air environments, leading to the formation of non-protective oxides that deplete the bulk alloy of Mn"

Mechanism with scope. Mechanism: Superior oxidation resistance at high temperatures due to the formation of Al- and Cr-rich oxide layers.. System: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy (as-cast and composite forms).. Conditions: High temperature exposure (specifically mentioned at 1100 °C for the as-cast alloy).. Evidence: inferred. Observation: The declining oxidation rate at 1100 °C is attributed to the formation of protective Al, Cr-rich oxide layers, making the composite a promising high-temperature structural material.. Scope limits: The text cites this property for the as-cast alloy and infers it for the composite, but does not provide new high-temperature oxidation test data for the composite itself in this paper.. Alternatives: Traditional RHEAs which generally possess poor high temperature oxidation resistance.. Quote: "In consideration of the superior oxidation resistance, the P/M NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy composite could be considered as a promising high temperature structural material."
